subtitle: How coins, scrolls and scripts bound a fractured frontier

panels.shot: epic close-up of a weathered silver Indo-Greek coin held between ink-stained fingers, one face showing Greek letters, the other Kharosthi signs, with faint silhouettes of mountains and stupas behind
panels.action: Gandharan Kharosthi Scribe holds up a gleaming Indo-Greek coin between thumb and forefinger in a dim scriptorium, distant Gandharan hills and a half-seen stupa looming beyond the window.

dialogue.text: On the northwestern frontier, a single coin spoke in two scripts—Greek and Kharosthi—binding kings, merchants and monks into one readable kingdom.

i18n.hi: उत्तर-पश्चिमी सरहद पर एक सिक्का दो लिपियों में बोलता था—यूनानी और खरोष्ठी—जो राजा, व्यापारी और भिक्षुओं को एक पढ़ने योग्य राज्य में जोड़ देता था।

panels.shot: wide aerial of the northwest subcontinent, from the Indus valley to Taxila, with caravan routes and rivers glowing faintly like veins
panels.action: A sweeping landscape shows rugged Gandharan mountains, the Indus river and roads converging on the bustling city of Taxila, caravans inching along like ants.

dialogue.text: This was Gandhara, where mountains met the Indus, and roads from Iran, Central Asia and the Ganga plain braided into the trading city of Taxila.

i18n.hi: यह था गंधार, जहाँ पहाड़ सिंधु से मिलते थे, और ईरान, मध्य एशिया और गंगा मैदान से आती राहें मिलकर तक्षशिला के बाज़ारों में घुसती थीं।

panels.shot: medium shot of rock face at Shahbazgarhi with neatly carved Ashokan edict lines, seen from a low angle against the sky
panels.action: An ancient rock surface at Shahbazgarhi fills the frame, its lines of Ashokan edict carefully incised in Kharosthi, with moss clinging in the grooves.

dialogue.text: A century earlier, Ashoka had carved his edicts here at Shahbazgarhi and at Mansehra, using Kharosthi to carry the Mauryan king’s words into the northwest.

i18n.hi: सदी भर पहले अशोक ने यहीं शाहबाज़गढ़ी और मानसहरा में अपने शिलालेख गढ़वाए, खरोष्ठी में, ताकि मौर्य सम्राट की वाणी उत्तर-पश्चिम तक पहुँचे।

panels.shot: close-up on a line of Kharosthi letters on the rock, then a ghosted overlay of a scribe’s hand copying them onto a palm leaf
panels.action: Kharosthi letters etched into stone sit in sharp focus, while a transparent image of a hand with a stylus hovers, echoing the script onto a slim leaf.

dialogue.text: Kharosthi ran right to left, tailored for Prakrit speech of the region. It became the script of officials, merchants and monks who needed to read the king.

i18n.hi: खरोष्ठी दाएँ से बाएँ बहती थी, यहीं की प्राकृत बोली के हिसाब से ढली। यह उन अफसरों, व्यापारियों और भिक्षुओं की लिपि बनी जिन्हें राजा पढ़ना था।

panels.shot: dynamic wide of a battlefield aftermath, Greek and Indian soldiers resting together with mixed gear and standards
panels.action: Exhausted Greek and Indian soldiers sit together near their stacked spears and shields under a banner bearing unfamiliar symbols, as dust from a recent campaign still hangs in the air.

dialogue.text: Then, from the northwest, Hellenistic kings pushed in. Indo-Greek rulers like Apollodotus and Menander took old cities but inherited the scribes and roads of Gandhara.

i18n.hi: फिर उत्तर-पश्चिम से हेलनिस्टिक राजा धकेलते हुए आए। अपोलोदोतुस और मेनान्दर जैसे इंडो-यूनानी शासकों ने पुराने नगर लिए, पर गंधार के लेखक और सड़के विरासत में पाए।

panels.shot: interior medium shot of a royal mint in Taxila, with furnaces in back and a central focus on Gandharan Kharosthi Scribe examining dies
panels.action: Inside a busy mint, Gandharan Kharosthi Scribe studies an engraved die on a workbench while artisans hammer blanks in the smoky background.

dialogue.text: To rule this layered land, they needed a language on metal. In the mints of Taxila, Greek officials and local Kharosthi scribes worked side by side.

i18n.hi: इस तहदार देश पर राज करने को उन्हें धातु पर भाषा चाहिए थी। तक्षशिला के टकसालों में यूनानी अफसर और स्थानीय खरोष्ठी लेखक कंधे से कंधा मिलाकर काम करने लगे।

panels.shot: tight close-up on two coin dies on the table, one engraved in Greek letters, the other in Kharosthi, with the scribe’s finger hovering between them
panels.action: On a wooden table, two metal dies lie side by side: one bearing crisp Greek legend, the other carefully cut Kharosthi, as Gandharan Kharosthi Scribe’s ink-dark fingertip points between them.

dialogue.text: The solution hardened in silver: one face in Greek, the other in Kharosthi, stating the same royal claims in two scripts.

i18n.hi: हल चाँदी में जड़ गया: एक तरफ यूनानी, दूसरी तरफ खरोष्ठी, दोनों में वही शाही दावा दोहरी लिपि में लिखा।

panels.speaker: kharosthi_scribes
panels.shot: medium profile shot of Gandharan Kharosthi Scribe speaking to an unseen Greek official, gesturing toward a sketch of coin legends
panels.action: Gandharan Kharosthi Scribe, seated cross-legged, holds up a wax tablet with mirrored lines of Greek and Kharosthi, addressing a shadowed figure in a Greek cloak.

dialogue.text: Greek letters named the Basileus, the king, for soldiers and settlers. Kharosthi carried ‘Maharajasa’ for merchants, taxmen and villagers along the Indus.

i18n.hi: यूनानी अक्षरों ने सैनिकों और बसने वालों के लिए बासिलियुस यानी राजा का नाम उकेरा। खरोष्ठी में ‘महारजस’ बहती रही—सिंदु किनारे के व्यापारियों, महसूलियों और गाँववालों के लिए।

dialogue.speaker: kharosthi_scribes
dialogue.text: Two scripts, one ruler. Then all who trade his coins will know him.

i18n.hi: दो लिपियाँ, एक शासक। उसके सिक्कों से सौदा करने वाला हर कोई उसे जान लेगा।

panels.shot: montage-style wide shot of different hands receiving and using coins: a Greek soldier, a local trader, a monk
panels.action: Three vignettes share the frame: a Greek soldier’s gloved hand taking pay; a bearded trader counting coins at a stall; a robed monk accepting a small donation at a stupa.

dialogue.text: The same coin clinked in a soldier’s palm, crossed a trader’s stall, and dropped into a monk’s bowl, its twin scripts silently repeating the king’s name.

i18n.hi: वही सिक्का कभी सिपाही की हथेली में खनकता, कभी व्यापारी की दुकान पार करता, तो कभी भिक्षु के भिक्षा–पात्र में गिरता—दोहरी लिपि चुपचाप राजा का नाम दोहराती रहती।

panels.shot: close-up of a silver coin of Apollodotus rotating in mid-air, one side freezing on Greek legend, the flip freezing on Kharosthi
panels.action: A silver Indo-Greek coin spins in the air; at one pause its Greek lettering and royal portrait are clear, at another the Kharosthi legend curves around a symbol.

dialogue.text: Under Apollodotus, under Menander, the pattern hardened into habit. Bilingual coinage became systematic—an administrative practice made visible in every purchase.

i18n.hi: अपोलोदोतुस के नीचे, मेनान्दर के नीचे, यह ढर्रा आदत में जम गया। द्विभाषी सिक्के एक पक्का दफ्तरशाही चलन बने—हर ख़रीद में दिखने वाली राजकाज की प्रथा।

panels.shot: wide marketplace scene in Taxila, with a money-changer’s table as the focal foreground and different scripts visible on weights and tallies (without readable letters)
panels.action: In a bustling Taxila bazaar, a money-changer sits behind a low table piled with mixed coins, while assistants tally transactions on wooden counters and palm slips.

dialogue.text: Markets learned to trust these little bilingual oaths of metal. Every deal turned the coin over and over, Greek and Kharosthi scripts confirming the face was not a fraud.

i18n.hi: हाट–बाज़ारों ने इन दो–भाषी धातु–कसमें पर भरोसा करना सीख लिया। हर सौदे में सिक्का बार–बार पलटता—यूनानी और खरोष्ठी देख–देखकर तय होता कि चेहरा नकली नहीं।

panels.shot: moody wide shot of a stupa complex in Gandhara at dusk, with caravans arriving and departing
panels.action: At dusk, a Gandharan stupa rises above a monastery courtyard as caravans arrive with creaking carts, while robed monks move between stone railings and shade trees.

dialogue.text: Around the stupas of Gandhara, merchants brought Indo-Greek coins as gifts. The coins spoke of kings; the stupas and monasteries spoke of the Buddha.

i18n.hi: गंधार के स्तूपों के आस–पास व्यापारी इंडो–यूनानी सिक्के दान में लाते। सिक्के राजाओं की भाषा बोलते, स्तूप और विहार बुद्ध की।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot of a monastery scriptorium with Gandharan Kharosthi Scribe and a young monk seated among birch-bark strips
panels.action: Inside a cool stone cell, Gandharan Kharosthi Scribe and a young monk sit among narrow birch-bark strips, an oil lamp casting warm light as they prepare inks and styluses.

dialogue.text: The same Kharosthi that carried royal names now traced sacred words. Birch bark strips, scraped and joined, became a new page for Gandhari-language teachings.

i18n.hi: यही खरोष्ठी जो कभी शाही नाम ढोती थी, अब पवित्र शब्द बुनने लगी। भुर्ज–पत्र की पट्टियाँ खुरचकर, जोड़कर गंधारी उपदेशों के नए पन्ने बन गए।

panels.shot: close-up of Gandharan Kharosthi Scribe’s hand writing Kharosthi on a birch-bark scroll, with a faint overlay of a coin in the background
panels.action: Gandharan Kharosthi Scribe’s hand leans close to the bark, drawing firm Kharosthi characters, while in the shadowed background the outline of a coin seems to glow faintly.

dialogue.text: On these narrow scrolls, scribes wrote in Gandhari, a local Prakrit. The orthography they used grew out of the same script-world that had served kings and traders.

i18n.hi: इन पतली स्क्रॉलों पर लेखक गंधारी, स्थानीय प्राकृत, लिखते। उनकी लिखावट उसी लिपि–दुनिया से उगी थी जो पहले राजाओं और व्यापारियों की सेवा करती थी।

panels.shot: dramatic archaeological cut: an excavated clay jar broken open, revealing tightly rolled, fragile birch-bark scrolls
panels.action: In a modern excavation trench, a cracked clay jar lies opened to reveal tightly rolled, fragile birch-bark scrolls nestled within the dust.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, in the late twentieth century, jars of birch-bark scrolls from this region emerged in the modern world, their Kharosthi letters still legible.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद, बीसवीं सदी के उत्तरार्ध में, इसी क्षेत्र के भुर्ज–पत्र स्क्रॉलों के घड़े दुनिया के सामने आए—उनकी खरोष्ठी अब भी पढ़ी जा सकने वाली थी।

panels.shot: modern scholarly study shot: a conservator under magnification gently unrolls a scroll, with reference diagrams of Kharosthi characters on the desk
panels.action: In a laboratory, a conservator carefully teases open a brittle scroll under a magnifying lens, while sheets with hand-drawn Kharosthi signs lie arranged nearby.

dialogue.text: Scholars like Richard Salomon and Andrew Glass traced these Gandhari manuscripts, studying how each Kharosthi character rendered sound, word and formula.

i18n.hi: रिचर्ड सैलोमन और एंड्र्यू ग्लास जैसे विद्वानों ने इन गंधारी पांड–पत्रों की लड़ी पकड़ी, देख–देखकर कि हर खरोष्ठी अक्षर कैसे ध्वनि, शब्द और सूत्र रचता है।

panels.shot: split panel: on one side, an ancient Kharosthi inscription; on the other, a Gandhari manuscript line, both tied by a faint map of Gandhara overlay
panels.action: A vertical split shows a weathered stone inscription on one side and a close-up of flowing Kharosthi on birch bark on the other, with a faint outline of Gandhara’s map connecting them.

dialogue.text: They found continuity, not a single act of patronage: an administrative habit of Kharosthi writing that flowed naturally into a manuscript culture for Buddhist learning.

i18n.hi: उन्हें टू–टी–सी परंपरा नहीं, बल्कि निरंतर धारा मिली: खरोष्ठी लेखन की एक दफ्तरशाही आदत, जो सहज बहते–बहते ही बौद्ध शिक्षा की पांडुलिपि–संस्कृति में घुस गई।

panels.shot: low-angle medium shot of Gandharan Kharosthi Scribe seated between a stack of coins and a pile of scrolls, lit by cross-light from coin shine and lamp glow
panels.action: Gandharan Kharosthi Scribe sits at a low table; to one side neatly stacked coins catch a cool glint, to the other bundled scrolls glow in lamplight as he gazes between them.

dialogue.text: Kharosthi scribes never ruled armies. Yet by giving kings two scripts on one coin, and monks a script for their scrolls, they made a diverse frontier legible to itself.

i18n.hi: खरोष्ठी लेखक ने कभी सेनाएँ नहीं चलाईं। पर एक ही सिक्के पर राजाओं को दो लिपियाँ देकर, और भिक्षुओं को उनकी स्क्रॉल के लिए लिपि देकर, उन्होंने इस बहुरंगी सरहद को खुद अपने लिए पढ़ने योग्य बना दिया।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot: Gandharan Kharosthi Scribe walks along a stupa railing at dawn, while a lone coin lies half-buried in the path
panels.action: At pale dawn, Gandharan Kharosthi Scribe walks slowly along the stone railing of a stupa; in the dusty path before him, an Indo-Greek coin lies half-buried, its twin scripts faint but present.

dialogue.text: In Gandhara, power learned to write itself twice so that many could read it; today, those twin scripts remind us that diversity becomes governable when people can read the words that rule them.

i18n.hi: गंधार में सत्ता ने खुद को दो बार लिखना सीखा, ताकि ज़्यादा लोग उसे पढ़ सकें; आज वही जुड़वाँ लिपियाँ याद दिलाती हैं कि विविधता तभी राजकाज में बदलती है, जब लोग अपने ऊपर लिखे हुए शब्द पढ़ सकें।

subtitle_i18n.en: How coins, scrolls and scripts bound a fractured frontier
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे सिक्के, स्क्रॉल और लिपियाँ ने टूटे सरहद को बाँधा
